subject: Pegasus P0: tokens/sec absorption & safety-lane plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Pegasus P0: tokens/sec absorption & safety-lane plan

Team — looping you in on Pegasus (DEAL-7834). They asked for a concrete plan that ties their projected request profile to a Dedicated slab recommendation and an operational safety lane (burst capacity / graceful degradation) so procurement can sign a 12‑month commit next week. High level notes from call: average payloads ~220 tokens, peak session chains up to 1,200 tokens (multi-turn), expected peak qps ~45 for a 2‑hour daily window. Their SLO: p95 generation latency <= 450ms for the chosen model family.

Preliminary numbers I sketched below — please sanity-check and make any adjustments before I send PSG and legal the mutual action plan:

- Model variant: Mistral-8B-q4f16 (quantized fit they've validated)
- Avg tokens per request: 220
- Peak requests/sec (observed in pilot): 45 rps
- Peak tokens/sec = 45 * 220 = 9,900 tokens/sec
- Our measured tokens/sec per GPU (Mistral-8B-q4f16, 1xA100 equivalent slab, warm KV cache): ~4,000 tokens/sec steady; cold-start ~2,400 t/s
- Raw GPU count to meet peak (no headroom) = ceil(9,900 / 4,000) = 3 GPUs
- Target operating headroom = +50% for burst + KV cache variability = 3 * 1.5 = 4.5 => recommend 5 GPUs in slab
- Expected p95 at 5 GPUs (with warm cache & batching): ~320ms; p99 estimated ~520ms.

Questions for engineering/solutions:
1) Does the 4,000 t/s steady figure look right for our current runtime baseline for Mistral-8B-q4f16 (batching, prefix cache warm)? Any regional hardware caveats?
2) Can we present a fallback policy (auto‑route to smaller variant or queueing) that guarantees p95 <= 450ms when hot capacity is exhausted?
3) Ops: how long to spin up the +2 burst GPUs if we do a burst pool? (target < 6 minutes)

Attachments: I exported their sample requests, token histogram, and my quick calc (attached). I can draft the customer-facing page after we lock the numbers.

Next: Ben/Prio/Karthik — please reply with adjustments and an ops-safe recommendation by EOD PST so I can finalize the mutual action plan for their procurement sync tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pegasus P0: tokens/sec absorption & safety-lane plan

Thanks Jasmine — good baseline. Quick comments from infra side after running a matching microbenchmark last week:

- 4,000 t/s steady is optimistic for multi-tenant A100 pods in us-west unless we guarantee isolated slab topology; 3,200 t/s is safer for our current kernel selection with sequence lengths averaging 220 and 16‑step prefix cache warmups.
- Cold cache penalty tends to be around 30–40% for these request chains; your cold-start number (2,400 t/s) matches previously observed behavior.
- For a hard SLO at p95 = 450ms, I wouldn't rely solely on headroom. Recommend a two-pronged plan:
  a) Dedicated slab sized to absorb 120% of expected peak (not 50%): ceil(9,900 * 1.2 / 3,200) = ceil(11,880 / 3,200) = 4 GPUs in slab.
  b) Burst pool (cross-tenant warm thin pool) sized for incremental 40% traffic for sustained spikes — pre-warmed group of 2 GPUs that can be dropped into the route until full slab scales.
- Fallback policy: auto-route requests above 6s queue time to a smaller variant (Mistral-4B-q4) with response trimming + function-calling suppression; typical p95 there ~280ms for these tokens but quality delta acceptable for non-core flows.

Operational ask: ops needs a confirmed placement (us-west1) and a canary window to validate cache warm behavior. If procurement wants a hard SLA on p95 < 450ms, legal will demand clear fallback and burst sizing.

I attached a quick scratch calc and suggested config. Priyom — can you validate the customer impact of falling back to Mistral-4B for non-critical endpoints?

-Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of operational knobs and a short calculation from my side.

Assumptions summary (from pilot samples + Ben's numbers):
- Pilot peak tokens/sec: 9,900 t/s
- Safe per-GPU steady throughput (us-west1, dedicated topology): 3,200 t/s
- Cold start / cache miss factor: 1.35 (i.e., throughput drops to ~2,370 t/s)

Capacity math I recommend we show to the customer (concise):
- Base slab: 4 dedicated GPUs (absorbs ~12,800 t/s at steady)
- Safety lane / burst: 2 pre-warmed GPUs in a dedicated burst pool (cover ~6,400 t/s steady) but practical absorption during burst ~4,500 t/s because of cross-tenant sharing assumptions
- Total available (design): base + burst = nominal 7,200–12,800 t/s range depending on cache state; effectively absorbs the 9,900 t/s peak with headroom and accounts for cache churn

SLO fit statements we can include in the mutual action plan:
- With 4 GPUs + 2 burst + warm cache, expected p95: ~300–380ms (meets customer p95 <= 450ms).
- If cache cold or burst pool exhausted, auto-fallback to Mistral-4B keeps p95 <= 480ms for non-critical endpoints; for critical flows we plan request shedding and queuing with progressive degradation.

Operational notes:
- Warm-prep time for the burst pool (spin-up + weight propagation) = ~5 minutes if we keep the burst pool partially filled and use quick prober hooks.
- I recommend a 30-day canary: week 1 validate token distribution and cache warm behavior, week 2–4 calibrate batching and KV TTLs, then ramp to full commit.

I've uploaded the csv of token histograms and a polished SLA calculation sheet (see attachments). I'm fine drafting the short paragraph for procurement that states: "Redwood recommends a 4 GPU Dedicated slab in us-west1 with a 2 GPU pre-warmed burst pool; fallback and request-shedding policies are documented in the attached runbook."

-Priyom
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

This plan looks good and I'm comfortable signing off on the numbers for procurement with the following conditions:

1) Ops will provision the 4 GPU Dedicated slab in us-west1 and configure the 2 GPU burst pool as pre-warmed but subject to a daily keepalive policy (to avoid cold eviction). Ops to confirm cost delta for pre-warm.
2) Engineering will prepare the fallback matrix: auto-route >10s queue to Mistral-4B + request trimming. We must document quality delta and which endpoints are eligible.
3) Solutions to own the 30-day canary timeline and provide weekly readouts (token distributions, p95/p99, cache hit ratio).

Jasmine — go ahead and update the mutual action plan: recommend "4x Dedicated GPUs (us-west1) + 2x pre-warmed burst GPUs; canary 30 days; fallback to Mistral-4B for non-critical routes." Call out p95 expectation: 300–380ms with warm cache.

I will ask finance to prepare the committed pricing term sheet; procurement will want that inserted into the MOU. Once you share the final MAP, I'll route for legal sign-off.

Thanks — Karthik
VP, Product & Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
